description:
## Why

All SQLite tables that store per-message state (mailboxes, messages, article numbers, overview, flags, change log, subscriptions) currently assume a single user. Multi-user requires each table to be scoped to a user_id.

## What

Add user_id column and update primary keys / indexes for:

- mailboxes table: (user_id, mailbox_id) PK
- messages table: (user_id, message_id) — or per-user message_number within a mailbox
- article_numbers: (user_id, group_name, article_number) PK
- overview: (user_id, group_name, article_number) PK
- user_flags: already has user_id — verify it is correctly scoped
- state / change_log: (user_id, ...) PK
- subscription_store: (user_id, ...) PK

Write SQLite migrations for each table. All queries in the corresponding store modules gain a user_id parameter.

Block store (CIDs) is NOT per-user — blocks are shared across users (content-addressed dedup). Only the metadata tables are per-user.

## Acceptance

- All store modules accept user_id at the query boundary
- Two users can have independent mailboxes with the same article stored once in the block store
- Migrations run cleanly on existing single-user databases (existing rows assigned to the default user_id=1)
notes: The block store sharing is important for storage efficiency — if alice and bob both receive the same email, it is stored once as a CID and both users have a metadata row pointing to it.
title: Per-user storage isolation in SQLite
